item.title: Blues cop blow ahead of BOG
item.description: KHELVIN Engineering Lautoka FC has been dealt a blow ahead of the upcoming tournament after striker Veleni Rasorewa was suspended by Fiji Football. Lautoka FC president Shalendra Prasad confirmed to The Fiji Times that the club had received notification from Fiji Football that Rasorewa had been suspended for breaking camp during the Fiji U19 programme.
item.content:encoded:
KHELVIN Engineering Lautoka FC has been dealt a blow ahead of the upcoming tournament after striker Veleni Rasorewa was suspended by Fiji Football.

Lautoka FC president Shalendra Prasad confirmed to The Fiji Times that the club had received notification from Fiji Football that Rasorewa had been suspended for breaking camp during the Fiji U19 programme.

“This is disappointing news for us. He is one of our deadly strikers and now he is suspended,” Prasad said.

“However, we welcome the decision by Fiji Football. Veleni was part of our 22-member squad.”

The Men in Blue have been in camp for the past five days under the guidance of their new coach, Solomon Islander Batram Suri.

“The team has been in camp for five days and has been training daily and trying their best,” Prasad said.

The 2024 Battle of the Giants champions expect a tough competition, with Prasad saying the side is not underestimating any of its opponents.

“It will be a good competition. We do not underestimate any team. All teams are good, and it will be a good competition come the weekend,” he said.

New coach Batram Suri will guide Lautoka FC into BOG and IDC in Suva next month. His playing career included representing the Solomon Islands and featuring for Nadi FC in Fiji.

He has since coached Solomon Islands age-group national teams and club sides, including Ifira Black Bird and Galaxy FC from Vanuatu, and most recently guided Galaxy FC at the 2026 OFC Men’s Champions League held in Fiji.

item.title: Golfers set for two-day tournament in Suva
item.description: THE R.C. Manubhai Fiji Golf Open returns to the Suva Golf Club this weekend, with another strong field expected for the two-day tournament. The annual tournament will be held this Saturday and culminates on Sunday and is expected to attract experienced golfers, emerging talent and members of the wider golfing community.
item.content:encoded:
THE R.C. Manubhai Fiji Golf Open returns to the Suva Golf Club this weekend, with another strong field expected for the two-day tournament.

The annual tournament will be held this Saturday and culminates on Sunday and is expected to attract experienced golfers, emerging talent and members of the wider golfing community.

Around 140 golfers took part in last year’s event, with Shakil Pillay winning the overall title and Ashish Chand finishing runner-up.

The tournament has become a major fixture on Fiji’s golfing calendar and continues to grow in popularity each year.

R.C. Manubhai Group Marketing Manager Chetna Ben said the company was pleased to see the tournament return and continue its long-standing association with the sport.

The company has a proud history of supporting golf in Fiji, having sponsored the Ba Golf Club Open for more than 56 years.

This makes its sponsorship one of the longest-running private sporting sponsorships in the Pacific.

R.C. Manubhai Group CEO Dr Uppiliappan Gopalan said the company’s support for sporting events was about more than corporate visibility.

“We are proud to once again support the R.C. Manubhai Fiji Golf Open. Golf brings together people from different backgrounds through a shared appreciation for skill, discipline and sportsmanship.

“We are honoured to contribute to an event that strengthens community spirit and supports the continued development of the sport in Fiji.”

Dr Gopalan said the tournament reflected R.C. Manubhai’s broader commitment to supporting initiatives that create meaningful and lasting value for local communities.

Through its partnership with the Fiji Golf Open, R.C. Manubhai aims to encourage participation in sport while promoting unity, discipline, sportsmanship and stronger community connections.

The company has extended its best wishes to all participating golfers and acknowledged the Suva Golf Club, organisers and supporters for their contribution towards the tournament.

Another competitive weekend of golf is expected when players tee off at the Suva Golf Club on Saturday.

item.title: North in spotlight
item.description: THE North has produced another rising football talent, with 14-year-old Dreketi College goalkeeper Meresiana Sukanauwa earning a late call-up to the Fiji Mini Kulas squad for the OFC U-16 Women’s Championship in Solomon Islands. Sukanauwa’s selection comes just a fortnight after she won the Golden Glove in the Open Girls grade at the Extra Fiji Secondary Schools Football Championship in Labasa.
item.content:encoded:
THE North has produced another rising football talent, with 14-year-old Dreketi College goalkeeper Meresiana Sukanauwa earning a late call-up to the Fiji Mini Kulas squad for the OFC U-16 Women’s Championship in Solomon Islands.

Sukanauwa’s selection comes just a fortnight after she won the Golden Glove in the Open Girls grade at the Extra Fiji Secondary Schools Football Championship in Labasa.

Her rise is significant not only for Dreketi College, but for Northern football, as she becomes the first member of her family to represent Fiji in football.

Remarkably, Sukanauwa only started playing football in Year Eight and was initially a reserve goalkeeper for Dreketi College.

Teacher and coach Mohammed Altaf said giving her an opportunity during the school’s second zonal pool match proved decisive.

“She was on the bench, but in our second zonal pool game, I decided to give her an opportunity because I believed she was capable of doing the job,” Altaf said.

Sukanauwa seized the opportunity, saving a penalty and helping Dreketi College protect a 2–1 lead.

“From that moment, she continued to improve and showed that she had the ability and confidence to become a good goalkeeper,” Altaf said.

Her performances earned her the Golden Glove before the unexpected national call-up.

“It was a proud moment for me and my school when I received the Golden Glove award, and it has become even sweeter now that I have been called into the Mini Kulas squad,” Sukanauwa said.

Altaf described her as “very hardworking and courageous” and said she never gave up.

Sukanauwa will now carry the hopes of her school, family and the North onto the international stage.

item.title: Rigamoto sets sights on Fiji call-up
item.description: AFTER two painful championship defeats, Eli Rigamoto finally has his national title — and now the Yat Sen captain wants to take the next step and wear the Fiji colours. For Eli Rigamoto, winning the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Basketball National Championships under-17 title was not the end of the journey.
item.content:encoded:
AFTER two painful championship defeats, Eli Rigamoto finally has his national title — and now the Yat Sen captain wants to take the next step and wear the Fiji colours.

For Eli Rigamoto, winning the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Basketball National Championships under-17 title was not the end of the journey.

The Yat Sen Secondary School captain led his side to a convincing 27-12 victory over International School Suva at the Vodafone Arena last week, but his thoughts have already turned towards a bigger challenge — earning selection for Fiji.

Rigamoto, a Year 11 student who has been at YSS throughout his secondary education, has set his sights on making the national under-17 team and continuing his progression through Fiji’s age-grade pathway.

“Yes, I’m hoping to enter the under-17 national team next year and for many years to come,” he said after the final.

For Rigamoto, representing Fiji is an ambition that extends beyond the U17 grade.

He wants to progress through the national age grades before eventually pushing for a place in the senior team.

The confidence comes from seeing basketball grow around him.

Rigamoto believes the sport is beginning to establish itself at YSS, despite rugby remaining the dominant sport in Fiji.

“Basketball in Yat Sen, it’s starting to be a major sport,” he said.

He believes that growth can eventually translate into success beyond Fiji.

While acknowledging that Fiji is not yet widely recognised as a basketball nation, Rigamoto sees no reason why that cannot change.

“I see it developing in many years to come,” he said.

His immediate challenge, however, is keeping the winning culture alive.

Next year, Rigamoto and his teammates will move into the U19 grade with the confidence of national champions.

“I can’t wait,” he said. “Every year, it is very exciting to look forward to.”

The title carried extra weight for the young captain.

Before last week’s triumph, Rigamoto had experienced the disappointment of losing two previous championships.

“For the past two years, I’ve been schooling. I’ve lost two championships.”

That pain made the victory even sweeter.

Rigamoto credited his teammates, parents, teachers and supporters for helping the team get over the line, but the captain knows the hard work is only beginning.

The national U17 crown has given him a taste of success.

Now he wants Fiji to taste it on the international stage.

item.title: Young shuttlers make mark
item.description: THE Inaugural Primary School Badminton Tournament came to an exciting close yesterday at the FMF Gymnasium, with 22 schools from across Viti Levu battling for honours. Young shuttlers from years four to eight took to the courts throughout the tournament, displaying their skills, determination and competitive spirit as they represented their respective schools.
item.content:encoded:
THE Inaugural Primary School Badminton Tournament came to an exciting close yesterday at the FMF Gymnasium, with 22 schools from across Viti Levu battling for honours.

Young shuttlers from years four to eight took to the courts throughout the tournament, displaying their skills, determination and competitive spirit as they represented their respective schools.

The tournament provided a valuable platform for budding badminton players to gain experience and test themselves against some of the best young talent from around Viti Levu.

Yat Sen Primary School emerged as the winners of both the girls’ and boys’ team competitions, creating history in the competition.

item.title: Coach backs the process
item.description: THE Vodafone Fijiana XV head coach Willie Walker says success for the national women’s side will not be measured by the scoreboard alone as the team prepares for a one-off Test against Japan on September 4. The Fijiana XV squad left the country on Tuesday night for the Japan Test before travelling to Hong Kong for the WXV Global Series Challenger, which will be held from September 13 to 26.
item.content:encoded:
THE Vodafone Fijiana XV head coach Willie Walker says success for the national women’s side will not be measured by the scoreboard alone as the team prepares for a one-off Test against Japan on September 4.

The Fijiana XV squad left the country on Tuesday night for the Japan Test before travelling to Hong Kong for the WXV Global Series Challenger, which will be held from September 13 to 26.

Walker said the team’s priority was to build the right processes throughout the week and ensure the players are fully prepared before match day.

“For us, we don’t want to focus on winning. Winning is a by-product of making sure we’ve done everything that we can throughout the week to prepare as much as we can to give us a chance to win,” Walker said.

The coach believes preparation from one week in Nadi is what ultimately gives the team an opportunity to perform on the weekend in Japan.

He said the players must understand that success comes from consistently doing the small things correctly rather than simply turning up on match day.

Walker also acknowledged the importance of support from Fijian fans as the team prepares for a challenging period of international rugby.

He urged supporters to continue backing the players while understanding that improvement is part of the team’s long-term journey.

He said the players understood that supporters were behind them and would do everything possible to represent the Fijiana emblem with pride.

Against Japan, Walker expects a fast and disciplined opponent that will challenge Fiji for the full 80 minutes.

He said Fijiana XV must remain patient, control possession, defend strongly and build phases if it is to create scoring opportunities.

For Walker, the goal is to establish a strong process that can deliver results both now and in the future.

Fiji has played Japan only once, and Walker expects a physical contest against a side he describes as strong, fast and committed.

item.title: St Anne’s girls eye top-30
item.description: SAINT Anne’s Primary School (SAPS) will make its third consecutive appearance at the Zespri AIMS Games in Tauranga, New Zealand, with its under-13 netball team setting its sights on improving last year’s 53rd placing. SAPS U13 netball coach Makitalena Takayawa said the team was determined to climb the rankings after finishing 53rd among more than 100 schools at last year’s tournament.
item.content:encoded:
SAINT Anne’s Primary School (SAPS) will make its third consecutive appearance at the Zespri AIMS Games in Tauranga, New Zealand, with its under-13 netball team setting its sights on improving last year’s 53rd placing.

SAPS U13 netball coach Makitalena Takayawa said the team was determined to climb the rankings after finishing 53rd among more than 100 schools at last year’s tournament.

“Last year, they placed 53 out of 100 plus schools and our goal this year is to move from 53 up to 40s, top 30s,” Takayawa said.

She said the main objective was for the girls to enjoy the experience while improving their position.

“As long as the girls enjoy themselves and move our rank a little bit higher,” she said.

Takayawa, who is in her second year at St Anne’s, said the school had been invited to the tournament each year and the girls were looking forward to returning to Tauranga.

The AIMS Games, held annually in Tauranga, provides young athletes with an opportunity to compete against schools from across New Zealand and the Pacific.

Netball has been St Anne’s main sport at the tournament, with the school taking its under-13 team each year.

This year, the school will also make its mark in badminton, with Abigail Corrie set to represent St Anne’s in the sport.

Takayawa said getting the team to New Zealand had required considerable support from parents and the wider St Anne’s community.

“This trip has really been a testing one and we couldn’t do this without God and the support of our parents has been so wonderful.”

She acknowledged the efforts of parents who came together for last-minute fundraising, as well as donations from the St Anne’s alumni, the school community and supporters in Fiji and abroad.

Their support, she said, had helped the team prepare for the trip.

The 2026 Zespri AIMS Games will be held from September 5-11 and will bring together school-aged athletes from New Zealand and the Pacific.

item.title: Tailevu turns focus to Rewa
item.description: FRESH Choice Tailevu Rugby Union has little time to celebrate its narrow victory over Naitasiri, with attention already turning to another important round 6 Skipper Cup clash against Rewa this week. Tailevu secured a 27-25 win over Naitasiri at Nakelo last week, a result that kept the side in third place on the points table.
item.content:encoded:
FRESH Choice Tailevu Rugby Union has little time to celebrate its narrow victory over Naitasiri, with attention already turning to another important round 6 Skipper Cup clash against Rewa this week.

Tailevu secured a 27-25 win over Naitasiri at Nakelo last week, a result that kept the side in third place on the points table.

President Joseph Rodan said the team’s ability to fight until the final stages was again crucial in the victory.

“Our boys played 80 minutes,” Rodan said.

“We were down by a few points, and our team came right in the last minute and scored.”

The result has given Tailevu confidence as it prepares to face Rewa at the same venue.

Rodan said the team had continued to show improvement and was now competing at a higher standard.

He also credited the coaching and management staff for preparing the players to maintain their effort throughout the matches.

“We have been doing this for the last four games. It just goes to show that our coaches and managers are doing the right thing to get the points,” Rodan said.

Tailevu’s third-place position puts further importance on the upcoming match as teams continue to battle for valuable points.

Rodan also urges supporters to play their part when Rewa visits Nakelo this weekend.

Tailevu will be hoping its strong finish against Naitasiri can be repeated when it takes on Rewa on Saturday, September 5 at Nakelo School grounds.
